notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (gate exit 0; evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). This package is model-authored by deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 (run ros-wave-c-128) and unreviewed: driver.lock.json keeps reviewed_by null. No human review, no hardware attachment, no hardware backend, no real MuJoCo run, no Isaac Sim run and no ROS graph run is claimed.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card is family:ros with RosDriver, but the pinned clone is a robot-description and asset repository, not a ROS control runtime. Its README describes an Isaac Sim workflow (README.md:3-37); the piper_description CMakeLists only installs launch, meshes, rviz, urdf and mujoco_model directories and defines no executable (piper_description/CMakeLists.txt:1-38); the manifest declares no message, service or action (piper_description/package.xml:3-24); the display launch starts only robot_state_publisher, joint_state_publisher and rviz2 (piper_description/launch/piper_with_gripper/display_urdf.launch.py:23-60); the only controller reference is a gazebo_ros2_control plugin whose parameters live in piper_gazebo/config/ros2_controllers.yaml, a package and file absent from this clone (piper_description/urdf/piper_description.xacro:531-535). There is therefore no pinned ROS endpoint or type to bind, and a RosDriver cannot express this repository. The package instead serves the card's models[0], piper_description/mujoco_model/piper_description.xml, as a configuration-only MujocoDriver: device mhs://localhost/piper-isaac-sim, kind world.sim, mode simulated, risk R0 (the card's floor). cap.world.step.v1 applies {ticks, action: {ctrl: [...]}} to data.ctrl and runs mj_step; cap.world.reset.v1 runs mj_resetData + mj_forward. The card's second model, piper_no_gripper_description.xml, is not served (one package serves one model).

MODEL AND LIMITS: the MJCF is a fixed-base chain of six hinge and two slide joints with eight position actuators (piper_description/mujoco_model/piper_description.xml:1-70); every actuator sets ctrllimited=true with an explicit ctrlrange (:60-69), so the bridge derives action.ctrl from those ranges at run time and refuses an out-of-range element before writing data.ctrl. The derived intervals are joint1 -2.618..2.618, joint2 0..3.14158, joint3 -2.697..0, joint4 -1.832..1.832, joint5 -1.22..1.22, joint6 -3.14158..3.14158, joint7 0..0.0475 and joint8 -0.0475..0. The package declares no Limit and no operator-required bound, so no site-limits.example.json is needed. The model's joint1 joint range ends at 2.168 while its actuator ctrlrange ends at 2.618; the driver publishes the ctrlrange exactly as the MJCF states it and neither widens nor narrows it. The model file and its meshes are read in place from the read-only clone; nothing is copied or imported.

FAKE: MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed where the gate runs, so backends['fake'] is this package's pure Python stand-in mujoco module, .fake:FakeMujoco. It parses the pinned MJCF for the eight joints (eight qpos and eight qvel) and the eight actuator ctrlranges, but its integration is a placeholder first-order motion toward the control target and it loads no mesh, contact, equality, tendon, actuator dynamics or sensor. The model's <position> actuators are position servos; the stand-in is not that servo and ignores forcerange, damping, inertia and joint limits. It exposes no mj_getState/mj_setState/mj_stateSize, so the bridge uses its basic checkpoint profile. The MJCF declares no <option timestep>, so the fake uses MuJoCo's library default 0.002 s as a placeholder; the reported 2.0 ms is the fake's value, not a line of the clone. Only the fake backend is declared; the real MuJoCo path is the family's lazy import for a backend name outside backends, needs mujoco and the model's mesh assets, and was not run. There is no hardware backend.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps the required mhs.testing.check_driver(HERE, backend='fake') call and adds ten cases (model shape, four ctrlrange refusals with zero effect, accepted boundary values, step advancing time and moving joint2, step without an action, short ctrl refusal, reset to model defaults, snapshot/restore of the advertised state, fidelity contract, e-stop latch); all pass.

WARNINGS left by the last gate run, all expected and none failing: G1.CLONE_NOTE reports two tracked paths that share one file on this case-insensitive filesystem (piper_x_description/meshes/dae/base_Link.dae and base_link.dae); the gate's case-shared handling reports no modification and reads the pinned commit. G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because the simulator-family fake is the stand-in engine itself, not an upstream package class. G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the bridge-derived inputs ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed. PLAYBOOK.md section 8 treats these simulator-family warnings as expected. No G4.REF_VALUE, G4.REF_BINARY or G4 reference warning was raised.

LICENCE AND PUBLICATION: upstream licence_spdx is NOASSERTION and the piper_description manifest leaves its licence as a TODO declaration (piper_description/package.xml:8). The card has publish_review required; the owner decides before publication. This pass is not a publication decision.

NOT COVERED: the real MuJoCo engine, its contacts, constraints and actuator dynamics; the Isaac Sim USD assets and the Isaac Sim play workflow; the Gazebo/ros2_control route, whose controller config is absent; the no-gripper MJCF (models[1]); rendering, camera, inertial and sensor arrays; and any physical PiPER hardware. No catalogue_requests: only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 are used. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run. The clone at commit 8e1f88fdb7afca49c40e9a0c1c01cc588e86f0d2 was read only; the gate reported no modification. The digest above is the digest line of the last gate run.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the MujocoDriver deviation (the clone is a description and asset repository: Isaac Sim USDs, URDF/xacro and two MJCFs, CMakeLists that only install directories, no ROS node, topic, service or action), the model path and meshes, all 13 facts, the ctrlrange-derived step envelope (piper_description.xml:61-68), the stand-in fake and the lockstep latch, which does stop this simulation. Defects: the stand-in fake, which has no physics, published the real engine's F1 'mujoco:piper_description' contract, which a test asserted; two facts said more than their lines (a 'so ... no integration timestep' inference, a card-licence remark on package.xml:8); and the ctrlranges that exceed the joint ranges of joint1, joint4, joint6, joint7 and joint8 were noted for joint1 only. Reviewer changed driver.py (fidelity_by_backend publishes the fake as F0 'analytic:stand-in mujoco module (no physics)', the class-level F1 contract keeps the real-engine gaps, two facts narrowed, facts for the ctrlrange/range mismatch and the vendored realsense2_description Apache-2.0 manifest), test_driver.py (F0 on the fake, F1 on the class) and facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json; the gate and collect.py --strict pass with the expected MuJoCo-family warnings and the digest unchanged. The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: Simulation only: the package steps the PiPER MJCF in MuJoCo (never run here; the fake is a placeholder stand-in), not Isaac Sim, and the clone ships no hardware driver. The step envelope is the model's ctrlrange, wider than five joint ranges, so in-envelope targets drive joint1 (kp 10000, forcerange +-20000) or the gripper slides against their limits. Licence: the four PiPER description manifests say TODO, the vendored realsense2_description says Apache-2.0.
